title: How many CPE hours do registered tax and BAS agents need in Australia?
seoTitle: TPB CPE requirements for tax agents
description: Tax Practitioners Board CPE explained: 120 hours over 3 years for tax agents, 90 for BAS agents, 20 a year, conditional agents, records and renewal.
shortAnswer: The Tax Practitioners Board (TPB) requires registered tax agents to complete at least 120 hours of continuing professional education (CPE) over each three-year registration period, with at least 20 hours each year, and registered BAS agents to complete 90 hours with 20 each year. Conditional registrations carry lower minimums. Completing CPE that meets TPB requirements is a condition of renewal under paragraph 20-5(1)(d) of the Tax Agent Services Act 2009, and records must be kept for five years.
keyTakeaways: The current CPE requirements commenced on July 1, 2022 and are explained in TPB Guidance Statement TPB(GS) 37/2021.
Standard tax agents need 120 hours per 3-year period (20 a year); standard BAS agents need 90 hours (20 a year); conditional registrations range from 6 to 60 hours.
Paragraph 20-5(1)(d) of the Tax Agent Services Act 2009 makes completed CPE a renewal requirement, and Code item 30-10(8) requires agents to maintain relevant knowledge and skills.
No more than 25% of CPE should be technical or professional reading, and up to 10% may be educative health and wellbeing activity.
Records must be contemporaneous and kept for 5 years from the end of the CPE period. Members of recognized associations can rely on their association's CPE if it meets TPB minimums.
regulator: Tax Practitioners Board (TPB), under the Tax Agent Services Act 2009 (TASA)
appliesTo: Individual registered tax agents, including tax (financial) advisers registered with a condition
Conditional registrants such as quantity surveyors, fuel tax credit specialists and Australian financial services registrants
Accounting, bookkeeping and advisory firms that employ or supervise registered agents

sections.heading: Why is CPE mandatory for registered tax practitioners?

blocks.text: CPE is mandatory because the Tax Agent Services Act 2009 (TASA) makes it a condition of renewing registration. The TPB's [Guidance Statement TPB(GS) 37/2021](https://www.tpb.gov.au/tpb-gs-37-2021-cpe-requirements-tax-and-bas-agents) states that "Paragraph 20-5(1)(d) of the TASA imposes a mandatory obligation on all registered tax practitioners to have completed CPE that meets the TPB's requirements to renew their registration."

CPE also supports the Code of Professional Conduct in section 30-10 of the TASA. Subsection 30-10(8) reads: "You must maintain knowledge and skills relevant to the tax agent services that you provide." The guidance also cites subsections 30-10(10), on taking reasonable care to apply taxation laws correctly, and 30-10(12), on advising clients of their rights and obligations. Where the TPB finds a Code breach after an investigation under Subdivision 60-E, it can order the practitioner under section 30-20 to take specified actions, which may include completing a course of education or training.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the TPB's continuing professional education page and TPB(GS) 37/2021 (last updated December 18, 2025) as at November 2026. The requirements have applied since July 1, 2022.

sections.heading: How many CPE hours does each type of registration need?

blocks.text: Minimum hours depend on the registration type and any condition on it. The TPB's [CPE page](https://www.tpb.gov.au/continuing-professional-education) sets out the following minimums for a 3-year registration period; shorter or longer periods are pro rated.

blocks.text: The guidance explains the reasoning: tax agents provide a wide scope of services and have mature CPE options, so 120 hours; BAS agents provide a narrower but expanding scope, so 90 hours; conditional practitioners may not provide a broad range of services and may have less relevant CPE available, so lower minimums apply. The regulations governing recognized associations set a different benchmark for their members: item 103(a) of Schedule 1 to the Tax Agent Services Regulations 2022 requires recognized BAS agent associations to have voting members undertake at least 15 hours of CPE each year.

sections.heading: When does the CPE period start, and can it be aligned with an association?

blocks.text: The CPE period is 3 years and begins on the date the practitioner registers with the TPB. A member of a recognized professional association can instead elect to align with the association's CPE period, based on a calendar year, financial year or membership anniversary.

No notice to the TPB is needed for the election, but the practitioner should note the elected period on their CPE log. Once elected, the period cannot be changed unless the practitioner moves to another recognized association, in which case a new election can be made at the end of the existing period. Members of associations such as CPA Australia and CA ANZ often align, which lets one log serve both; see [CPA Australia CPD requirements](/regulations/cpa-australia-cpd-requirements) and [CA ANZ CPD requirements](/regulations/ca-anz-cpd-requirements).

sections.heading: Which activities count as CPE for tax agents?

blocks.text: Activities must be relevant to the tax agent or BAS services the practitioner provides, but they are not limited to technical tax content. The TPB says practice management and ethics are also relevant, and it does not accredit CPE activities or prescribe topics.

items: **Structured activities** listed in the guidance include tertiary units, structured conferences and discussion groups including by video, seminars and webinars, podcasts and webcasts from an appropriate organization, writing or presenting technical publications or structured training, and structured in-house training by suitably qualified people.
**Knowledge of the TASA and the Code** is expected of all registered practitioners, and a unit of study on the TASA and Code can count as CPE.

**Reading limit:** the TPB expects that no more than 25% of CPE over the period comes from relevant technical or professional reading, which can include audio and visual resources. The TPB's [CPE activities](https://www.tpb.gov.au/cpe-activities) page notes that this cap was reinstated from January 1, 2023 after a pandemic relaxation.
**Wellbeing allowance:** up to 10% of CPE over the period can be educative health and wellbeing activity, such as webinars on stress management or self-care.

blocks.text: Recognized association membership simplifies the picture. If a practitioner complies with their association's CPE requirements, the TPB accepts that as meeting its own, provided the activities are relevant, delivered by suitably qualified people or organizations, and meet the TPB's minimum hours. Firms planning internal programs can map these rules into a [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) by registration type.

sections.heading: What CPE records does the TPB expect, and when are they checked?

blocks.text: Practitioners must keep a contemporaneous record and evidence of completed CPE, made as soon as practicable after each activity, showing the activity and the hours. The TPB publishes a CPE log in PDF and, since December 2025, Excel format. A log kept for a recognized association satisfies the TPB without a second record.

Records should be kept for 5 years from the end of the CPE period. The TPB requires confirmation of CPE at renewal and may request evidence at any time during the registration period. The TPB publishes compliance case studies, such as a [tax agent facing suspension for not completing CPE](https://www.tpb.gov.au/tax-agent-faces-suspension-not-completing-cpe). The general approach to audit-ready evidence is in [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: What if illness or caring duties prevent a practitioner from meeting the minimum?

blocks.text: The TPB will consider relief, but only if the practitioner shows they tried to use the flexibility of the 3-year period first. Its listed examples of extenuating circumstances are illness, disability, family or caring responsibilities such as maternity or paternity leave, and financial or other hardship, including a move to part-time work for those reasons.

The TPB's worked example describes a tax agent who completes only 5 hours in year one because of serious illness, then 55 and 60 hours in years two and three; the TPB accepts this as meeting the requirement despite the missed annual floor. Practitioners should keep records of the circumstances alongside the CPE log. The same refresh logic appears in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles), and firms in the [professional services sector](/industries/professional-services) often track TPB, association and AML/CTF training together.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each learning activity with its registration relevance, activity type and hours, so a firm can test the annual floor, the 25% reading limit and the 10% wellbeing allowance per practitioner before renewal. The same record can be exported as a CPE log covering the 5 year retention period.

faqs.q: Does the TPB approve CPE providers or courses?
faqs.a: No. The TPB does not accredit CPE activities or prescribe topics. Practitioners must judge whether activities are relevant to the services they provide and delivered by people or organizations with suitable qualifications or practical experience.

faqs.q: Can a tax agent rely on CPA Australia or CA ANZ CPD for the TPB?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are a member of a recognized professional association and comply with its CPE requirements, the TPB accepts that compliance, provided the activities are relevant to their tax agent services and meet the TPB's minimum hours for their registration type.

faqs.q: What happens if a registration period is not exactly three years?
faqs.a: The TPB says CPE should be completed on a pro rata basis where the registration period is other than three years. The annual minimum still applies to each year of the CPE period unless extenuating circumstances justify relief.

faqs.q: How long must tax agents keep CPE records?
faqs.a: Five years from the end of the CPE period. Records should be made as soon as practicable after each activity and show the details and hours, with extra notes for unstructured activities such as technical reading.
